newsitem.title: GERMANY: GEC Alsthom aims to double sales in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: GEC Alsthom aims to double sales in 1996/97.

text.p: GEC Alsthom GmbH, German unit of France's Alcatel Alsthom and Britain's General Electric Co Plc, hopes to double sales this year thanks to its purchase of AEG's energy transmission business.
Sales in the current business year should total about three billion marks, up from 1.4 billion in 1995/96, spokesman Herbert Gienow told journalists on Tuesday.

Following the acquisition of the AEG units last spring, GEC Alsthom would now enter a consolidation phase and was unlikely to make major purchases in the next two years. But personnel reductions were unlikely, Gienow said.
He declined to name the purchase price for the AEG operations, which raised GEC Alsthom's workforce to nearly 10,000 from 5,700.
Net profit in 1995/96 dropped to 12.6 million marks from 34.9 million, while operating profit fell to 26 million marks from 61 million marks, mainly due to higher pension obligations, Gienow said.
With the approval of the French government, GEC Alsthom's Dutch parent is studying whether a merger with atomic power plant contractor Framatome would make sense, he said.
The German unit is also studying whether to restructure as an Aktiengesellschaft, but has no plans for a stock market listing, he said.
